title: Accelerate 第 1 章 · 加速 — 专业书籍精读 Book 38
title_en: Accelerate Ch 1 · Accelerate — Books Deep-Read Book 38

questions.question: 一家公司为了降低线上事故，把发布改成每季度一次、每次走三层审批。按《Accelerate》第 1 章，最可能的结果是？
options: 实际风险更高：每次批量巨大，一出事无从下手，于是更怕发、攒得更久
影响不大：交付表现主要由团队技术水平决定，与发布流程无关
速度变慢但稳定性提升：这是快与稳之间一个合理的取舍
事故明显减少：审批层级越多，每次变更在上线之前就能被拦下越多的问题
questions.explanation: 数据显示快与稳同向，不是跷跷板；机制在批量大小。少发慢发加审批是负循环，「审批越重，实际风险越高」是本章最反直觉的结论。
questions.question_en: To reduce production incidents, a company moves to quarterly releases with three layers of approval. Per chapter 1 of Accelerate, what is the most likely result?
options_en: Higher real risk: each batch is huge, failures are hard to trace, so the team fears releasing and waits even longer
Little effect: delivery performance depends mainly on technical skill, not on the release process
Slower but more stable: a reasonable trade-off between speed and stability
Clearly fewer incidents: more approval layers catch more problems in each change before it ships
questions.explanation_en: The data show speed and stability move together, not as a seesaw, and the mechanism is batch size. Releasing rarely behind heavy approvals is a vicious cycle; heavier approval means higher actual risk, the chapter's most counterintuitive finding.

questions.question: 一家公司拿到了成熟度模型的第 4 级认证，宣布转型成功。按本章主张的能力模型，问题在哪？
options: 转型应该直接照搬 Netflix 等领先公司的完整实践清单，而不是自己从头摸索
认证机构不够权威，应该改用国际上更认可的成熟度评级体系
改进不该有终点：应持续测出当前最弱的一环、专治它、再测量，路径因团队而异
第 4 级还不够，应该继续投入，直到拿到第 5 级认证再宣布成功
questions.explanation: 成熟度模型的毛病是终点思维、一刀切、量活动不量结果；拿到认证那天改进就停了。照抄 Netflix 的清单同样被本章否定，要找的是自己的约束点。
questions.question_en: A company earns Level 4 certification under a maturity model and declares its transformation complete. Under the capability model this chapter advocates, what's wrong?
options_en: The transformation should copy the practice checklists of leaders like Netflix rather than finding its own way
The certifying body isn't authoritative enough; switch to a more internationally recognized maturity scheme
Improvement has no finish line: keep measuring your current weakest link, fix it, measure again, with paths that differ by team
Level 4 isn't enough; keep investing until Level 5 certification before declaring success
questions.explanation_en: Maturity models suffer from end-state thinking, lockstep paths, and measuring activities rather than outcomes, so improvement stops the day the certificate arrives. Copying Netflix's checklist is also rejected; you need to find your own constraint.

questions.question: 管理层打算把四个交付指标写进各团队的绩效考核并横向排名。按本章的提醒，这样做的风险是？
options: 考核会让团队过于追求稳定，从而不敢发版，部署频率下降
这些指标太难测量，团队之间的数据口径无法统一，没法比较
指标会被刷：拆发布刷频率、收窄故障定义压失败率，它们本该是看趋势的诊断工具
四个指标之间互相冲突，考核任何一个都会让另外三个变差
questions.explanation: 一旦写进考核，Goodhart 定律立刻生效，人会去刷数字。作者本意是诊断工具，该按团队看趋势，不该横向排名或折算奖金。
questions.question_en: Management plans to put the four delivery metrics into each team's performance review and rank teams against each other. Per the chapter's warning, what's the risk?
options_en: Reviews will make teams overly cautious and afraid to release, so deployment frequency drops
The metrics are too hard to measure and definitions can't be unified, so teams can't be compared
The numbers get gamed: split releases to inflate frequency, narrow "failure" to cut the rate; they're meant as diagnostic trend tools
The four metrics conflict, so rewarding any one of them makes the other three worse
questions.explanation_en: Once tied to reviews, Goodhart's law kicks in and people game the numbers. The authors meant them as a diagnostic, read as per-team trends, not for cross-team ranking or bonuses.
